what: Combining signals into single data frame
title: Plotting signals in batch
text: ggplot2 expects single long data frame one row per sample, signals combined first. read_id column identifies read sample comes . Keep mind long reads produce large data frames (, 127,464 rows). longer reads, many reads, plotting interval start_sample end_sample considered.
code: signal_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(selected_ids), function(i) {   read_signal <- out[['signal']][[selected_ids[i]]]   data.frame(read_id = selected_ids[i],              # that is how time is rescaled to seconds              time = (seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / out[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],              pa = read_signal) }))  # keep facets in the requested read order signal_df$read_id <- factor(signal_df$read_id, levels = selected_ids)  head(signal_df, 3) #>                                read_id    time       pa #> 1 0e8e52dc-3a71-4c33-9a00-e1209ba4d2e9 0.00000 48.33975 #> 2 0e8e52dc-3a71-4c33-9a00-e1209ba4d2e9 0.00025 51.28519 #> 3 0e8e52dc-3a71-4c33-9a00-e1209ba4d2e9 0.00050 51.11193

title: Plotting signals in batch
text: facet_wrap() draws one panel per read. scales = "free_x", panel span full read length, current axis shared, signal levels can compared reads.
code: g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(signal_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa)) g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d") g.facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~read_id, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Calibrated signals of selected reads",                         x = "time [s]",                         y = "signal [pA]")  plot_reads <- g.base + g.line + g.facet + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()  print(plot_reads)

text: process_pod5() reads consecutive groups part_size reads passes group user-supplied function. signal = TRUE, function receives named list reads (metadata) signal (vectors named UUID). Everything function returns discarded, plots written files . one group held memory time. vignette, plots written temporary directory. real data,save_dir point permanent location. Note: process_pod5() always reads whole signals. long reads, function calling extract_pod5_signal() start_sample end_sample selected reads may better choice.
code: save_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "signal_plots") if (!dir.exists(save_dir)) {   dir.create(save_dir, recursive = TRUE) }

title: Plotting signals in batch
text: function writes one PNG file per read, named UUID: additional arguments given process_pod5() (save_dir ) passed function.
code: # writes one base R signal plot (png) per read in the group save_signal_plots_base <- function(batch, save_dir) {      for (i in seq_len(nrow(batch[['reads']]))) {     # signal vectors are named by UUID, so look them up by read_id     read_id <- batch[['reads']]$read_id[i]     read_signal <- batch[['signal']][[read_id]]      # open a png device; file named by read UUID with a _base suffix     grDevices::png(file.path(save_dir, paste0(read_id, "_base.png")),                    width = 1600, height = 600, res = 150)          # convert sample index to seconds     graphics::plot((seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / batch[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],                    read_signal,                    type = "l",                    col = "#3a414d",                    xlab = "time [s]",                    ylab = "signal [pA]",                    main = read_id)          grDevices::dev.off()   } # for i      return(invisible(NULL)) }  pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,                     FUN = save_signal_plots_base,                     part_size = 10,                     signal = TRUE,                     calibrated = TRUE,                     save_dir = save_dir) #> [2026-11-10 23:25:24.373543] Processing POD5 reads... #> [2026-11-10 23:25:30.285009] Done!  length(list.files(save_dir, pattern = "_base\\.png$")) #> [1] 42

title: Plotting signals in batch
text: approach applies ggplot2, plot saved ggsave():
code: # write one ggplot2 signal plot (png) per read in the group # FUN for process_pod5(), called once per group of reads save_signal_plots_ggplot <- function(batch, save_dir) {      # seq_len() skips the loop when a group has no reads   for (i in seq_len(nrow(batch[['reads']]))) {     # signal vectors are named by UUID, so look them up by read_id     read_id <- batch[['reads']]$read_id[i]     read_signal <- batch[['signal']][[read_id]]      # ggplot2 needs a data frame: one row per sample, time in seconds     read_df <- data.frame(time = (seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / batch[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],                           pa = read_signal)      # layered plot     g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(read_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa))     g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")     g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = read_id,                             x = "time [s]",                             y = "signal [pA]")      plot_signal <- g.base + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()      ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(save_dir, paste0(read_id, "_ggplot.png")),                     plot = plot_signal,                     width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 150)   } # for i   return(invisible(NULL)) }  pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,                     FUN = save_signal_plots_ggplot,                     part_size = 10,                     signal = TRUE,                     calibrated = TRUE,                     save_dir = save_dir) #> [2026-11-10 23:25:30.343513] Processing POD5 reads... #> [2026-11-10 23:25:39.5971] Done!  length(list.files(save_dir, pattern = "_ggplot\\.png$")) #> [1] 42

title: Plotting signals in batch
text: write plots subset reads, selection applied within function. example , reads exceeding 20,000 samples plotted: reads required large file, efficient select UUIDs read_pod5() metadata extract directly extract_pod5_signal(). , signals reads decompressed.
code: # writes base R signal plots only for reads longer than min_samples. # intended as FUN for process_pod5(), called once per group of reads save_long_reads <- function(batch, save_dir, min_samples) {   # flag reads in the current group exceeding defined sample threshold   keep <- batch[['reads']]$num_samples > min_samples   if (!any(keep)) {     return(invisible(NULL)) # no long reads there   }   # subset metadata only. Signal list is left as is, as vectors are looked up by read_id   batch[['reads']] <- batch[['reads']][keep, , drop = FALSE]   save_signal_plots_base(batch, save_dir)      return(invisible(NULL)) }  long_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "long_reads") if (!dir.exists(long_dir)) {   dir.create(long_dir, recursive = TRUE) }  pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,                     FUN = save_long_reads,                     part_size = 10,                     signal = TRUE,                     calibrated = TRUE,                     verbose = FALSE,                     save_dir = long_dir,                     min_samples = 20000)  length(list.files(long_dir)) #> [1] 11

code: g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(signal_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa)) g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d") g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Calibrated signal",                         x = "time [s]",                         y = "signal [pA]")  plot_signal <- g.base + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()  print(plot_signal) scale_levels <- c("raw [ADC counts]", "calibrated [pA]")  comparison_df <- data.frame(   position = rep(signal_df$position, 2),   signal = c(signal_df$raw, signal_df$pa),   scale = factor(rep(scale_levels, each = nrow(signal_df)), levels = scale_levels))  g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(comparison_df, ggplot2::aes(x = position, y = signal)) g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d") g.facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~scale, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Raw and calibrated signal",                         x = "position [samples]",                         y = NULL)  plot_comparison <- g.base + g.line + g.facet + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw() print(plot_comparison)
